Connecting ecologists with other disciplines grants

records.justification: The agent's text only captures the claim about global eligibility, omitting the requirements regarding permits, permissions, and the ecological science focus of the projects.

claims.text: Applicants are responsible for obtaining all relevant permits and permissions required to undertake the proposed work.
Projects must have a clear ecological science focus, with other aspects like sociology or economics clearly integrated into the ecology and scientific goals.
Researchers from all countries globally are eligible to apply.

claims.text: Applicants must be a BES member.

Research assistants are ineligible.
Postdoctoral researchers are ineligible.
Undergraduates are ineligible.
Master's students are ineligible.
Graduates who have completed their degree are ineligible.

No more than two applicants from the same institution may attend the same meeting or conference.

Work must be of relevance to the training course or meeting being applied to attend.
Applicants must give a presentation if attending a meeting (e.g., poster, workshop, plenary talk).

records.justification: The agent's text only captures a partial description of the eligibility criteria, specifically that individuals involved in teaching ecology at any level are eligible, but omits many other key eligibility requirements and the purpose of the grants.

claims.text: Applicants must be members of BES.

claims.text: No more than one grant will be awarded to any applicant in a year.
No more than two grants will be awarded to any applicant in any five years.
Grants must be for projects that meet at least one of the top-level BES aims.
Projects must communicate evidence-based messaging about ecology, how nature works, and the use of ecological science as a solution to challenges.
Projects must raise awareness and public understanding of ecological careers, their relevance, importance, breadth, diversity, and show that anyone can become an ecologist.
Projects must share how individuals can take action to benefit the environment, themselves, and society.
Projects must increase the ability of others to deliver the above aims through outreach and engagement activities.
Proposals must be aimed at a non-academic audience.
Projects must clearly demonstrate direct interaction with a non-academic audience.
Projects should show evidence of links to the research community at regional, national, and international levels, where appropriate.
Applications will not be considered for staff salaries (though one-off costs relevant to completing the event, such as sub-contracting for logo design, will be considered).
Applications will not be considered for training courses not associated with developing skills in communicating the science of ecology for a public-facing audience.
Applications will not be considered for projects aimed solely at delivering curriculum to school children.
Applications will not be considered for projects delivered to a small number (1-2) of schools in a school setting where other members of the public can’t engage.
Applicants must be BES members.
